messages:
marta: FYI ran mixed-precision bench on a prod-like load, saw ~18% p99 regression when switching to fp8 default kernel.
ashwin: hmm, can you paste the perf logs so we can see the breakdown?
marta: here's the run summary:
```
benchmark: bert-512-like
kernel: fp8_matmul_v2
batcher: continuous
p50 8ms  p95 32ms  p99 120ms  (+18% vs int8 baseline)
throughput: 210 tok/s -> 260 tok/s (op rate up) but tail latency increased
```
kevin: interesting — throughput up but tail latency up too. smells like padding / memcpy effects in the hot path.
jen: did KV cache hit rate change? fp8 path sometimes touches a different codepath for KV packing.
marta: KV hit rate steady at 0.93, but trace shows extra memcpy during kernel selection. snippet: 
```
select_kernel_for_shape(shape=(B, S), qtype=fp8)
-> quant_dispatch(fp8, int8_fallback)
-> if (!is_aligned(ptr, 32)) memcpy(aligned_buf, src, sz) // extra copy
```
ashwin: memcpy for alignment is a killer for p99. which shapes are hitting that?
marta: lots of traffic with seq_len in [1,64]. continuous batching pads to 64, and fp8 kernels require 32-byte alignment so odd lengths often force copy.
kevin: that explains throughput vs latency mismatch. more ops but added copy per request. two possible levers: change batching pad granularity or select an int8 kernel for small seqs.
jen: int8 kernel lacks the alignment-copy but has slightly worse quality on summarization tests unless we recalibrate.
marta: quick config experiment i ran locally:
```json
{"batching": {"mode": "continuous", "pad_to_multiple": 16, "max_batch_wait_ms": 20}}
```
kevin: good call — reduce pad waste and align to 16 cuts memcpy frequency. also consider pad_to_min_field to avoid jumping to next power-of-two.
ashwin: another idea: augment kernel-selection with a tiny cost model: estimate memcpy cost per-request vs faster fp8 matmul throughput and pick kernel per-(batch_shape, seq_len) at runtime.
jen: we'll need to track calibration drift too — forcing int8 for small seqs might avoid memcpy but could regress quality unless we re-run post-quant calibration.
perf-bot: benchmark run completed at 1745067903 -> patched config (pad_to_multiple=16) shows p99 down ~14% from the problematic run, p50 unchanged. full artifacts: https://ci.redwood/perf/1745067903
marta: great. action items: 1) add kernel-cost model (kevin) 2) add a runtime memcpy/tracer (ashwin) 3) schedule fp8 calibration sweep for small-seq workloads (jen) 4) roll out conservative batching config to canary (eng-sre)
kevin: I'll open the PR for kernel-cost model and include microbenchmarks per-shape.
ashwin: I'll prototype a lightweight memcpy tracer that tags align-copy occurrences in traces. microbench results will include per-call ns overhead.
marta: also adding a small script to synthesize worst-case shape mixes so CI can catch this class of regression: `scripts/bench_mixed_shapes.py --mix \"1:0.4,8:0.3,64:0.3\"`.
jen: will run calibration sweep and post results to this thread.
marta: tagging @eng-sre for rollout planning :eyes: 
kevin: :thumbsup:
